study.title: Enhanced Functional Connectivity between the Bilateral Primary Motor Cortices after Acupuncture at Yanglingquan (GB34) in Right-Hemispheric Subcortical Stroke Patients: A Resting-State fMRI Study
study.study_design: Cross-sectional with within-subject pre/post acupuncture comparison and between-group comparison (stroke patients vs. healthy subjects); resting-state fMRI and task-evoked fMRI
study.population: Twenty right-hemispheric subcortical stroke patients and 20 healthy subjects
study.disease_condition: Right-hemispheric subcortical ischemic stroke with left motor hemiparesis
study.inclusion_criteria: first-ever ischemic stroke; aged 35–75 years; subcortical lesion restricted to the right internal capsule (IC), basal ganglia (BG), corona radiate (CR), and its neighboring regions; within 6 months after the onset; without cognitive deficit
study.exclusion_criteria: recurrent stroke; any brain abnormalities; any other disease that may influence participation; any MRI contraindications

arms.dropouts: Two patients (subject 04 and subject 18) were ruled out for resting-state analysis, for exhibiting head motion >3 mm maximum translation and/or 3° rotation during the course of needling scans

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included in this study. The study compares only verum acupuncture (GB34) pre/post within stroke patients, and between stroke patients and healthy controls at baseline.
Deqi questionnaire results are mentioned but no numerical scores, subscales, or statistical comparisons for deqi intensity are reported. Only the absence of sharp pain is confirmed for all subjects.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures are not reported or assessed.

The paper states '18 patients and 20 controls were performed by needling at GB34,' meaning 18 stroke patients and 20 healthy controls received the acupuncture intervention (2 stroke patients excluded due to head motion). The n_analyzed_neuroimaging for stroke arm is therefore 18.

The paper states 'n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging = 38' but two patients were excluded post-acquisition for head motion. Baseline resting-state comparisons (stroke vs. healthy) use 18 stroke + 20 healthy = 38 subjects. However, all 40 subjects contributed to task-evoked fMRI analysis.

The seed region for FC analysis (right M1 at MNI 39, −33, 63) was extracted from pooled task-evoked data across all 40 participants. This combined patients and controls for seed definition, which may affect the interpretation of FC comparisons.

Cluster sizes (in voxels or mm3) for the FC results are not numerically reported for either the stroke vs. healthy contrast or the pre/post acupuncture contrast. Only peak coordinates and peak t-scores are reported.
The paper does not report correlation between clinical measures (FMA, NIHSS) and FC changes after acupuncture.
The depth of acupuncture insertion is reported as '2–3 cm,' but no numeric conversion to mm is given explicitly. depth_mm_numeric is left null accordingly.

Needle retention time (total time needle was in situ) is not explicitly reported beyond the 1-min manipulation plus 1-min resting epoch description. Whether needle was retained during the full 8-min post-acupuncture scan is unclear.
Filtering parameters (e.g., bandpass filtering of resting-state data) and global signal regression procedures are not reported.

The paper does not specify whether the coordinate space for the FC result coordinates (e.g., −3, −33, 54 and −27, −6, 60) was explicitly labeled as MNI in the results section. However, the methods state normalization into the MNI template, so MNI space is assumed for all reported coordinates.

Figure 2 (Motor task activation map) and Figure 3 (FC differences) show additional spatial extent information visible in color-coded brain maps. Exact cluster coordinates beyond the peak values reported in text cannot be extracted from the figure images.

The paper labels the figure contrast in Figure 3A as 'stroke patients and healthy subjects' with the t-score scale showing −7.09 minimum, consistent with decreased FC in stroke patients. The direction of the contrast (stroke < healthy) is confirmed by the peak t-score of −7.0946 in the text.
